question: Should ClawHub admit `promptly-prompt` as a plugin package, and under which catalog family and namespace after prompt-hook security review?
rationale: The request is not a source bug; it changes catalog trust by exposing a third-party local prompt hook, so automation cannot choose the product family or security acceptance boundary.

options.title: Keep open for catalog/security review
options.body: Maintainers review the upstream hook, namespace, package family, and supported publish path before deciding whether it can be listed.

options.title: Redirect to skill-only publishing
options.body: Treat this as a direct skill submission and keep the plugin issue open only if the author provides an OpenClaw-compatible package shape.

options.title: Decline plugin catalog admission
options.body: Close after maintainer review if the Claude prompt hook is not an OpenClaw plugin or does not meet catalog safety expectations.

recommendation.title: Keep open for catalog/security review
recommendation.body: Maintainers review the upstream hook, namespace, package family, and supported publish path before deciding whether it can be listed.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent package-catalog and plugin validation history makes this the best available routing owner for the catalog-family decision.
